newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: OECD chief cautious on prospects for WTO.
newsitem.headline: OECD chief cautious on prospects for WTO.

text.p: OECD Secretary-General Donald Johnston said on Wednesday he hoped next week's WTO meeting in Singapore would keep up the momentum of trade liberalisation, but cautioned against excessive expectations.

"What is important, in my judgment, is the question of impetus. I think what's very important is that the level of expectations not be too high," Johnston told reporters during a visit to New Zealand.

He said constant peer pressure between countries would nudge the trade agenda forward. But slow progress in freeing up telecommunications, maritime transport and financial services since the 1994 Uruguay Round accords showed that plenty of difficult areas remained.

"(In) all these areas, you just have to keep chipping away, but I think the attitudes are right," said Johnston, who will attend the inaugural meeting of the World Trade Organisation from December 9-13.

He said the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, which last week welcomed South Korea as its 29th member, expected Slovakia to be the next to join the OECD. It was also examining applications from Argentina and Russia.
The latter, especially, had "lot of work to do in many, many areas", to meet OECD criteria, for example for freedom of capital movements, capital markets liberalisation, and taxation.

"I must say the Russian application was very warmly received by everybody. Even though Russia's obviously a long way from satisfying the codes, it represented a strong statement of moving forward to a much more liberalised economy," he said.
